The '''TIE/ln space superiority starfighter''', also called the '''TIE/ln''' or simply the '''TIE fighter''', was the signature [[starfighter]] of the [[Galactic Empire]] and symbol of its [[Realspace|space]] superiority. Instantly recognizable from the roar of its [[Ion engine|engines]] as well as its unique design, the TIE/ln exuded Imperial power and prestige across [[the galaxy]], seeing use throughout the Empire's [[Imperial Era|reign]]. They were nicknamed '''Evil-Eyes'''<ref name="Aftermath" /> or '''Eye-balls'''<ref name="Alphabet Squadron">[[Alphabet Squadron (novel)|''Alphabet Squadron'']]</ref> by members of the [[New Republic]].<ref name="Aftermath" />

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|The standard TIE fighter is fast but flawed. No shields, no hyperdrive, and no life-support system reduces its mass for greater maneuverability. Has a pair of laser cannons mounted at the base of the cockpit.|[[Antoc Merrick]]|<ref name="Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref>}}
[[File:TIEFighter-SWRebelsBlueprints.png|thumb|left|250px|Technical drawing of a TIE/ln starfighter]]
The TIE/ln starfighter was a small, short-range fighter developed, manufactured, and mass produced by Sienar Fleet Systems (SFS). Developed by SFS company head [[Raith Sienar]],<ref name="Epic Battles" /> the basis for the TIE fighter could be traced back to [[Kuat Systems Engineering]]'s [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter|Alpha-3 Nimbus starfighter]], along with several other outmoded models from the Old Republic.<ref name="RO Visual Guide" /> Like their predecessors, TIE's employed two vertical wings similar in appearance to V-wing starfighters; however, the [[Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor|Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor]] bore even more similarities with its central cockpit pod, twin ion engines, and common weapons technology.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> Its official production name was the '''Twin Ion Engine "line edition" space superiority starfighter'''.<ref name="RO Visual Guide" />

The fighter's name is derived from its propulsion system, which was specifically designed to create a distinct noise so as to inspire fear in those who opposed the Empire.<ref name="TOWM" /> These were originally two [[P-s3 ion engine]]s, which would be replaced by twin [[P-s4 ion engine]]s by approximately [[14 BBY]].<ref name="EotG" /> These engines could expel charged particles along almost any vector, providing the TIE fighter with incredible maneuverability, and their lack of moving parts or high-temperature components made them easier to maintain: Imperial records indicated less than five percent of all TIE fighters lost were as a result of field attrition.<ref name="TOWM" /> Fuel for the engines consisted of a radioactive gas kept in pressurized fuel tankage located on the underside of the cockpit.<ref name="RO Visual Guide" /><ref name="TOWM" /><ref name="SWCVNE">''[[Star Wars Complete Vehicles, New Edition]]''</ref>

A TIE fighter's twin ion engines, combined with [[Maneuvering jet|W-401 maneuvering jets]], provided thrust and boosters capable of quickly adjusting the ship's direction. The TIE/ln featured vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) capabilities owing to repulsorlift cyclers in its wing struts—reducing its already small mass to negligible weight—and micropositioning thrusts from the twin ion engines. Furthermore, the lack of a [[hyperdrive]] and resultant navigational systems alongside extended life support and fuel combined to cut down the TIE's total mass.<ref name="RO Visual Guide" /><ref name="TOWM" />

[[File:TIE_target_FF7.png|thumb|left|180px|A Rebel T-65B X-wing starfighter in the sights of a TIE fighter's targeting computer]]
In order to reduce cost, mass and energy consumption while improving maneuverability, the TIE fighter lacked [[deflector shield]]s. It was armored with [[quadanium steel]] plating which was proof against hand-held [[blaster]]s<ref name="TOWM" /> (except in exposed areas such as the stabilizers<ref name="Empire Ascendant 1">{{StoryCite|story=Two Sides to Every Sortie|book=Empire Ascendant 1}}</ref>) but could be penetrated by direct hits from military-grade [[laser cannon]]s, heavy [[blaster cannon]]s, and micrometeor impacts. However the cockpit's spherical shape meant that glancing blows would be deflected away.<ref name="TOWM" /> TIE fighters were equipped with sensor jamming capabilities and could be retrofitted with additional [[electronic countermeasures]].<ref name="SWCVNE" /><ref name="Squadrons">''[[Star Wars: Squadrons]]''</ref><ref name="VP">''[[Victory's Price: An Alphabet Squadron Novel]]''</ref>

The fighter's black "wings" were in fact an array of twelve [[solar collector]]s, framed by rigid quadanium steel foil braces, that featured a micro-crenulated solar absorption surface.<ref name="RO Visual Guide" /><ref name="TOWM" /> From there, power would be pooled to the fighter's solar energy collection hub<ref name="RO Visual Guide" /> and then to its twin ion engines. Originally the wings also powered the fighter's armaments, but this was found to quickly drain the fighter of energy and negatively affected its maneuverability. These early fighters were later retrofitted with a dedicated generator to power the lasers, a feature that became standard on all [[TIE series|TIE fighters]].<ref name="TOWM" /> These wings also served as [[stabilizer]]s.<ref name="The Call Rebels Recon">{{RebelsRecon|cto9_9qNHZ0|#2.14: Inside "The Call" | Star Wars Rebels|sw_url=video/rebels-recon-inside-the-call}}</ref>

The wings were sturdy enough to double as landing gear, further reducing overall mass, however, TIE fighters were designed to be deployed and retrieved using special cycling racks. Standard on Star Destroyers and other Imperial facilities, each rack system had a maximum capacity of 72 fighters. Beyond allowing pilots and technicians to access the craft more easily, the system was also equipped with small [[tractor beam]] projectors to assist with landing operations.<ref name="TOWM" /><ref name="SWCVNE" />

One drawback to the wing design was that it did obscure the pilot's field of vision, yet Imperial authorities considered this an acceptable motivation for pilots to concentrate on the targets in front of them.<ref name="TOWM" /> Due to its importance as a stabilizer, if part of the wing were to be removed to increase sight it would cost the fighter stability, which would then hamper the ship's ability to engage in dog fights.<ref name="The Call Rebels Recon" /> The wings did provide some measure of additional protection for the cockpit, and the fighter's sensor array compensated for the blind spots by augmenting and expanding the pilot's visual range.<ref name="TOWM" />

[[File:TIEFighter3-CoverArt.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Imperial TIE fighters]]
The TIE/ln was first and foremost designed for space combat, and while capable of operating in a planetary atmosphere it was at a distinct disadvantage versus other starfighters like the X-wing. The hexagonal wings made it harder to steer and more vulnerable to crosswinds. If it attempted to reverse its thrust too hard in order to decelerate, the fighter also risked causing severe structural damage to the wing spars and support pylons.<ref name="TOWM" /> However, depending on the circumstances the TIE fighter could still give a good account for itself in atmospheric combat. When operating down in tight urban confines and an oxygen-rich atmosphere for example, a TIE fighter was equal to an X-wing in speed and maneuverability.<ref name="VP" /> At higher altitudes it could also successfully engage in dogfights with X-wings at supersonic speeds.<ref name="Shadow Fall">''[[Shadow Fall: An Alphabet Squadron Novel]]''</ref>

The TIE fighter's primary armament was a pair of [[L-s1 laser cannon|L-s1 low-temperature laser cannons]] capable of destroying a [[Taylander shuttle]] in a single shot,<ref name="DB MG Fighter">{{Databank|mining-guild-tie-fighter|Mining Guild TIE fighter}}</ref><ref name="Legacy">{{Rebels|Legacy (episode)}}</ref> although by the time of the [[Battle of Endor]] these had been replaced with [[L-s7.2 laser cannon]]s. The green blaster bolt these weapons fired was the result of the more expensive [[blaster gas]] used by the Empire and aided pilots in identifying their shots. Mated to the cannons was an advanced [[T-s8 targeting computer]]—later replaced by the [[T-s9a targeting computer|T-s9a]] model—which was considered superior to the [[targeting computer]]s on Rebel fighters.<ref name="TOWM" /> As all combat craft were equipped with some form of [[sensor jammer]] equipment, the targeting computer cut down on the amount of time needed to obtain a "target lock," although for best performance they required constant readjustment by the pilot.<ref name="SWCVNE" /> While TIE fighters lacked any secondary weaponry as standard, they could be retrofitted to carry additional armaments such as [[missile]]s or replace their normal laser cannons with other models or [[ion cannon]]s.<ref name="Squadrons" />

Its central cockpit was tightly fitted, incorporating flight controls, viewscreens, targeting systems, tracking equipment—including a [[homing beacon]] in case the vessel was stolen—and room for a [[Imperial Starfighter Pilot|pilot]] all in the central pod. Despite being designed for a single occupant, several other passengers could fit inside the central cockpit, although the fit would be extremely tight.<ref name="Fighter Flight" /> A pressurized seal allowed the cockpit to retain an atmosphere and minimal, perfunctory oxygen scrubbers to protect the equipment, but the lack of any [[life support]] system required pilots to wear special [[TIE pilot flight suit|flight suit]]s and vacum-sealed [[flight helmet]]s. The onboard [[Flight data recorder|data recorder]], kept within an armored compartment beneath the pilot's seat, was designed to survive any event which would otherwise reduce the TIE fighter to scattered debris to allow for later retrieval and analysis.<ref name="TOWM" />

Flight controls were considered intuitive and easy to learn, in some cases allowing rebel novices to fly and operate them after having stolen them from Imperial airfields. TIEs were also outfitted with an [[ejector seat]].<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> Equipped with an antigrav unit and automated safety system, the seat was designed to guide the pilot away from debris and prevent any serious injury such as spinal fractures by determining when to release restrains or deploy the parachute. It was also equipped with a locator beacon to aid in pilot recovery.<ref name="TOWM" />

During the reign of the Empire, TIE fighters were favored for their versatility, if not for their durability. They were able to operate both in space as well as in planetary atmospheres, acting as fighters or scouts.<ref name="Spark">''[[Star Wars Rebels: Spark of Rebellion]]''</ref> They were more than capable of enforcing Imperial law against unarmed or lightly defended civilian transports. TIE/ln pilots were not afforded the independence enjoyed by equivalent pilots of the Rebel Alliance, as [[capital ship]]s were preferred for tactical discussion among the Imperial Starfleet.<ref name="RO Visual Guide" /> In Imperial doctrine, individual TIE fighters were used for scouting while a pair of fighters would be used to escort shuttles and other craft. A group of four TIE fighters, called a sentry group, was deployed to patrol the area around an Imperial ship or facility. A typical attack [[squadron]] consisted to 12 TIE fighters, and six squadrons together made up a full [[Fighter wing|attack wing]] of 72 fighters.<ref name="SWCVNE" />

At least a month after the [[Battle of Jakku]], all TIE/ln starfighters possessed by the [[Queluhan Nebula Imperial remnant]] were upgraded with advanced weaponry invented by [[Ved Foslo]], allowing them to punch through an enemy fighter's shields as well as hull, destroying them in a single hit.<ref name="Lost Stars" />

==History==
===A day to come===
In [[82 BBY]],<ref name="Date 82">''[[Dooku: Jedi Lost]]'' establishes that the [[mission to Asusto]] took place immediately following the [[funeral of Countess Anya]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[82 BBY]].</ref> the [[Padawan]] [[Dooku]] faced down numerous [[Force vision|visions]] of possible futures thanks to the [[torture]] he sustained at the hands of the [[Presagers of Hakotei]] during a [[mission to Asusto]]. In one vision,<ref name="Dooku: Jedi Lost">''[[Dooku: Jedi Lost]]''</ref> a TIE fighter swooped past before the vision shifted into a space battle between TIE fighters and [[X-wing starfighter]]s,<ref name="ScriptJedi Lost">[[Dooku: Jedi Lost (script)|''Dooku: Jedi Lost'' script]]</ref> which was only one of the many battles the young Dooku watched unfold. Later, [[Jedi Master]] [[Lene Kostana]] attempted to ease Dooku's worries about the futures he foresaw, letting him know nothing in them was a certainty.<ref name="Dooku: Jedi Lost" />

===Era of the Empire===
====Development process====
{{Quote|The Emperor insists that the Imperial starfighters should be economical for mass production, and designed to make pilots simultaneously dedicated and compliant. And above all, the Emperor wants our starfighters to incite fear.|Grand Moff Tarkin, in a memorandum to Raith Sienar|<ref name="TOWM" />}}
Following the transformation of the Galactic Republic into the authoritarian Galactic Empire<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> in [[19 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> Republic era weapons and equipment would continue to be utilized throughout the Imperial sphere. As time went by, the Republic's Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor and [[Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 starfighter|ARC-170 starfighters]] began to be phased out roughly five years after the [[proclamation of the New Order]].<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> The Empire's regional Governor of the [[Outer Rim Territories]], [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], commissioned [[Sienar Fleet Systems]] to create a line of single-pilot, short-range starfighters for the [[Imperial Navy]]. Tarkin mandated that the weaponized fighters should be extremely fast and maneuverable, energy efficient, and inexpensive to manufacture.<ref name="TOWM" />

Building off the advancements in starfighter engineering seen during the [[Clone Wars]],<ref name="Databank TIE fighter" /> Raith Sienar personally designed the fighters, basing them off designs from the [[Star Courier]], Alpha-3 ''Nimbus''-class V-wing starfighter, and the Eta-2 ''Actis''-class light interceptor. The result was a central spherical pod positioned between two hexogonal solar energy-collecting wings. To minimize power drain and maximize maneuverability, Sienar eschewed typically standard systems such as deflector shields and a hyperdrive. The [[TIE fighter prototype]] was created during the development process. After a series of test flights, the Empire approved Sienar's design, and executed an exclusive contract with Sienar for the production of TIE fighters.<ref name="TOWM" /> First seeing use in [[18 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> TIE fighters began to roll off assembly lines, with the Imperial mechanic [[Willard Waylin]] working on the TIE line since the beginning of their deployment,<ref name="Squadrons" /> and were ready for deployment by the time of the [[invasion of Mon Cala]], an event<ref name="Dark Lord 13">[[Darth Vader (2017) 13|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 13]]</ref> in 18 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]<ref name="Timelines" /> intended as a showcase of Imperial might, such as through the deployment of the Empire's new starfighters.<ref name="Dark Lord 13" />

====Across the stars====
[[File:Uprising_LoadingScreen_Item_Stormtrooper_Crop.png|thumb|left|200px|TIE fighters stationed at an Imperial airfield]]
The TIE fighter became a defining symbol of Imperial domination over its usage.<ref name="SilverCollectible">{{SideshowCite|set=Silver Collectible|pack=TIE / SF Blueprint|link=collectibles/star-wars-tie-fighter-sf-blueprint-agoro-914688}}</ref> With TIE pilots instructed to ignore their own well-being in order to achieve their objectives, the fighters were extremely fragile and their pilots expendable. With the Imperial Navy's vast size and unchallenged reign over the galaxy, the use of swarm tactics and subsequent mass production and refreshment of the vessels barely put a dent into Imperial manpower and industrial capacity. The low cost of production also spurred the craft's use.<ref name="RO Visual Guide" /> As a result, many features were sacrificed to facilitate mass production by Sienar Fleet Systems factories. Wilhuff Tarkin, an excellent pilot in his own right, was known to think very poorly of the TIE fighter due to its cramped cockpit and seemingly disposable nature.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /><ref name="tarkin">[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']]</ref> Imperial fighters also acted as psychological deterrents to potential seditious activities, with their roaring engines inspiring fear in those who heard them, leading to Imperial commanders to order their pilots to purposely fly low over areas that needed reminding of Imperial might.<ref name="Lost Stars" />

Waylin would meet TIE pilots over his career as he worked on the ships and was always impressed by their refusal to back down, figuring that the ship design's drawbacks built character.<ref name="Squadrons" /> As part of the five-year plan for the industrialization of the [[Outer Rim Territories]], TIE fighters were produced on a number of [[planet]]s, including [[Lothal]].<ref name="Empire Day">{{Rebels|Empire Day (episode)}}</ref> The Empire also gave some of its TIE fighters to loyalist companies to help secure its interests, leading to variants such as the [[TIE/mg Mining Guild starfighter|Mining Guild TIE fighter]].<ref name="DB MG Fighter" /> TIE fighters were deployed to put down the [[Moraysi rebellion]] and succeeded, with one TIE pilot in the engagement the former [[TK stormtrooper]] [[Ubrik Adelhard]]. Adelhard would go onto rise through the Imperial ranks, reaching the position of [[Grand Moff]] in time.<ref name="Insurgency 1">[[Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising 1|''Battle of Jakku — Insurgency Rising'' 1]]</ref>

===Rise of the Rebellion===
{{Quote|They're insanely quick. Maneuver like an angry wasp. And, oh yeah, they outnumber us ten to one.|A Rebel pilot|<ref name="Dark Visions 4">[[Vader - Dark Visions 4|''Vader - Dark Visions'' 4]]</ref>}}
[[File:Its_a_TIE.png|thumb|right|300px|TIE fighters at the [[Aldhani Garrison]]]]
While the Empire's rule was absolute for years,<ref name="Front Lines">''[[Star Wars: On the Front Lines]]''</ref> rebels had begun to arise as early as a year into its reign<ref name="Ahsoka">[[Ahsoka (novel)|''Ahsoka'']]</ref> and an [[early rebellion against the Galactic Empire]] was waged. The [[Spectres]] fought Imperial forces, including TIE fighters, on Lothal<ref name="Out of Darkness">{{Rebels|Out of Darkness}}</ref> and later joined with the [[Phoenix Cell]].<ref name="The Siege of Lothal">''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Siege of Lothal]]''</ref> In [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines" /> [[Mon Mothma]] [[Declaration of the Rebel Alliance|brought various rebel cells together]] as the Alliance to Restore the Republic.<ref name="Secret Cargo">{{Rebels|Secret Cargo}}</ref> While TIE fighters could engage unarmed and slightly defended civilian transports, they faced a more formidable foe in the form of the Alliance's starfighters.<ref name="RO Visual Guide" />

TIE fighters were stationed at a starfighter factory on the [[Supply moon]] while it was visited by [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and the [[Unidentified Imperial minister|then incumbent]] [[Minister of War (Galactic Empire)|Minister of War]]. As the factory was attacked by forces of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] it engaged their fighters but was ultimately destroyed.<ref name="Dark Visions 4" />

[[File:Displate-TIEFighter.png|thumb|left|350px|TIE Fighters tried and failed to defend the first Death Star at the Battle of Yavin]]
Following the destruction of the first [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]], the classification between [[Imperial Army|Army]] and Navy pilots—referred to as ground-hogs and vac-heads respectively—was rescinded, and the Imperial Military was to undergo a mass reorganization.<ref name="LCZA" /> After the Rebels [[Hijacking of the Harbinger|hijacked]] the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Harbinger (Imperial I-class)|''Harbinger'']], [[Luke Skywalker]] and [[Sana Starros]] use the stolen TIE fighters to patrol as the disguise for sign of Rebels, even no sign of the Empire.<ref name="SW 23">[[Star Wars (2015) 23|''Star Wars'' (2015) 23]]</ref>

Over time, a variety of other models arose from the TIE line, including notable vessels such as the [[TIE/IN interceptor]], [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE/sa bomber]], [[TIE/sk x1 experimental air superiority fighter]], [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter]], and the [[TIE/rp Reaper attack lander]], partly in direct response to faster and newer vessels manufactured by the Rebel Alliance. A variety of sub-models of the [[TIE series]] had arisen throughout Imperial history, with Sienar factories experimenting with localized improvements, producing advanced models suited to flying in local conditions and incorporating secret technological breakthroughs. Ships such as the [[TIE/ad v1]] fighter would see use by [[Baron of the Empire|flight barons]] and high-ranking members of the [[Inquisitorius]], however its extreme cost would later relegate its successor, the [[TIE Advanced x1]], to be flown only by elite pilots and members of the Imperial hierarchy such as Lord Vader.<ref name="Ultimate Star Wars" /> By the time of the [[Battle of Endor]], TIE/IN Interceptors made up 20% of the Empire's starfighter fleet.<ref name="SWEoSaOV">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia of Starfighters and Other Vehicles]]''</ref>

[[File:SWRebels_Imperial_TIE_Airfield.jpg|thumb|right|250px|TIE fighters on a Lothal airfield]]
Following the Battle of Endor, Imperial supply shortages would hinder the production and further development of TIE/ln starfighters, forcing [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]] to make do with an inadequate number of ships and inexperienced pilots.<ref name="Aftermath" />

Production data was classified, but according to numerous estimates, Sienar manufactured a minimum of approximately 4.6 million Imperial TIE fighters for [[Star Destroyer]]s, other Imperial Naval vessels, and Imperial [[garrison]]s and defense stations. Most estimates maintain that more Imperial TIE fighters were operational at the same time than any other starfighter in history.<ref name="TOWM" />

===Legacy===
[[File:TIEsfFighter-CGSWG.png|thumb|200px|left|The First Order Special Forces TIE/sf was the evolution of the TIE/ln fighter.]]
The legacy of the TIE fighter was not forgotten on the galactic stage, with Sienar Fleet System's successor, [[Sienar-Jaemus Fleet Systems]], producing the latest-generation TIE fighters utilized by the Empire's successor state, the [[First Order]]. The [[TIE/sf space superiority fighter]] and [[TIE/fo space superiority fighter]] were a direct continuance of the imprint the TIE fighter had on galactic citizenry, and featured advanced weapons systems and a two-seated arrangement for use by the Order's [[First Order Special Forces|Special Forces]].<ref name="ICS">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

The [[Ugnaught]] [[Kuiil]], himself former indentured servant of the Empire,<ref name="Chapter 7">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 7: The Reckoning}}</ref> used a [[Kuiil's workbench|workbench]] built out of an abandoned TIE cockpit.<ref name="100 objects">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref> Future historians would argue that flaws inherent in the TIE fighter design were allowed to remain, if only to increase the Empire's dependency on Sienar Fleet Systems for continued production of the craft, along with increased dependency on [[Kuat Drive Yards]] capital-scale carrier ships.<ref name="Propaganda">''[[Star Wars Propaganda: A History of Persuasive Art in the Galaxy]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:TIEmodels_btm.jpg|thumb|left|250px|TIE fighter models being constructed for ''A New Hope'']]
[[Industrial Light & Magic]]'s (ILM) Colin Cantwell created the concept model that established the TIE fighter's ball-cockpit and hexagonal-panels design for ''A New Hope''.<ref name="tiebts">{{WebCite|url=http://atthamovies.com/star-wars-tie-fighters|text=Star Wars TIE Fighter|work=Atthamovies.com|archivedate=20190422220354}}</ref> Sound designer [[Ben Burtt]] created the distinctive TIE fighter sound effect by combining an elephant call with a car driving on wet pavement.<ref name="Star Wars: The Power of Myth">''[[Star Wars: The Power of Myth]]''. DK Publishing, 2000.</ref>

The original TIE/ln fighters seen in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']] were relatively white, but were originally meant to have a maroon hull. One of the benefits of a slightly reddish color would have been that the fighter models would not have been as prone to "blue spill" as gray models were during filming against a blue screen. However, film composition tests revealed that the maroon ships blended too quickly into the mostly black star field when moving away from the camera, so a light gray was used instead.<ref name="Gizmodo">{{WebCite|url=http://gizmodo.com/5703593/the-original-tie-fighters-were-purple|text=The Original TIE Fighters Were Purple|work=Gizmodo|archivedate=20170609012208}}</ref> The TIE fighter models featured in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] were blue-gray.

Combat scenes between TIE fighters and the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' and Rebel Alliance [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing fighters]] in ''A New Hope'' were meant to be reminiscent of [[Wikipedia:World War II|World War II]] dogfight footage; editors used World War II air combat clips as placeholders while Industrial Light & Magic completed the movie's special effects.<ref name="empireofdreams">Burns, Kevin, and Edith Becker (2004) ''[[Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy]]''.</ref>

TIE/ln fighters are one of two starships available to Imperial players in ''[[Star Wars Battlefront]]'', the other being the TIE/IN interceptor. Compared to the X-wings and [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor|A-wings]], TIE fighters lack shields but instead possess good maneuverability and speed. However, their large wing panels make them very easy to hit in dogfights, giving Rebel fighters a slight advantage in ship-to-ship engagements.

[[File:TIE-Fighter-RO-SWCT.png|thumb|right|A TIE/ln as depicted in ''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'', which featured a transparisteel window that was noticeably smaller than those seen in ''A New Hope''.]]
''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' stated that TIE fighters built on Lothal had shorter wings, as explanation for stylistic choices made for the TIE/ln's design in the animated series ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]''. However, {{SW|url=video/rebels-recon-inside-always-two-there-are|text=Rebels Recon: Inside "Always Two There Are"}} said that there is no difference. Since then, [[Pablo Hidalgo]] confirmed on Twitter that ''Ultimate Star Wars'' was incorrect.<ref name="Pablo Hidalgo Tweet">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/678278140599271424|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Add that to Lothal TIE fighters, B-wing history and a Hego Demask reference that shouldn't be in there...|nobackup=1}}</ref>

TIE fighters later appeared in the [[2016]] anthology film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. Their animation model in the film featured noticeably smaller transparisteel windows<ref name="RO Visual Guide" /> that what was seen in prior ''Star Wars'' works, such as ''A New Hope''.<ref name="Episode IV" /> The 2016 reference book ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' by Pablo Hidalgo was the first reference book to identify the TIE fighter as the TIE/ln space superiority starfighter. It also defined the "ln" within the starfighter's name as standing for "line edition."<ref name="RO Visual Guide" />
